# AGENTS.md

Open Data Explorer (`opendata-explorer`) is an Angular single-page app
for MeteoSwiss's open government data (OGD). It lets end users browse and
download meteorological/climate data products, exploring station and asset
metadata served from a STAC (SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog) API and
visualizing them on a MapLibre GL map. State is managed with NgRx, UI
components use Angular Material, and translations run through Transloco.

## Commands

- `npm start` / `ng serve` — dev server at `http://localhost:4200`
- `npm run test-ci` — headless single run with coverage (`ng test --no-watch --no-progress --code-coverage --browsers=ChromeHeadless`)
- `npm test` / `ng test` — watch mode Karma/Jasmine; to run a focused subset, filter with Jasmine's `fit`/`fdescribe` in the spec rather than a CLI flag (Karma config has no per-file test path arg)
- `npm run lint` → `npm run type:check` → `npm run test-ci` is the effective CI order; run lint and type:check before tests when verifying a change
- `npm run format` / `npm run format:check` — Prettier over `./src`
- `npm run i18n:extract` then `npm run i18n:find` — regenerate/verify Transloco keys in `public/i18n`; `i18n:find` also runs in the pre-commit hook and fails the commit silently-ish (only prints a warning, doesn't block) if keys are missing/unused
- `npm run generate-stac-api` — regenerates `src/app/stac/generated/stac-api.generated.ts` from the MeteoSwiss STAC OpenAPI spec; never hand-edit generated STAC types
- `npm run build` — production build; output goes to `dist/browser/` (not `dist/<project-name>/browser/` — `outputPath` in `angular.json` is a plain string `"dist"`, and `@angular/build:application` writes straight into `dist/browser/` with no project-name segment). To verify the production build actually works locally (bypassing `ng serve`'s Vite dev-server, which can mask asset-resolution bugs that only reproduce in a real build): `npx http-server dist\browser -p 8080`, then open `http://localhost:8080`.
- Node version is pinned via `.nvmrc`

## Git hooks (Husky) — non-blocking but noisy

- `pre-commit`: runs `lint-staged` (eslint --fix + prettier on staged files, **this one does block the commit**), then checks branch name and translation keys — these two only print a warning, they don't fail the commit
- `commit-msg`: expects `MeteoSwiss/opendata-explorer#<issue-number>` somewhere in the message; only warns, doesn't block
- Branch name convention (warned, not enforced): `^(feature|hotfix|bugfix)/[0-9]+-[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$`, where the number is a GitHub issue reference and the trailing part is a short branch-name summary
- Commit message convention (warned, not enforced): end the message with `#<issue-number>`, referencing the same GitHub issue as the branch

## Naming & file conventions

- Avoid abbreviations; otherwise follow standard TypeScript naming.
- Services/components use the Angular `.service`/`.component` suffix; files are grouped by topic, shared files go in `shared/`.
- Type/interface definitions live in the `models` folder.
- Configs live in `src/app/shared/configs`; each config needs a matching interface in `models/configs`.
- Prefer configs over constants. If a constant is genuinely non-configurable, put it in the `constants` folder, scoped inside an exported `as const` object (not loose top-level exports).

## Testing

- Per repo convention, **components are intentionally not unit-tested** (UI testing is considered too brittle) — keep component classes thin. Services and NgRx effects/reducers/selectors must be tested.
- Coverage output goes to `coverage/meteoschweiz-opendata-explorer`.

## Architecture pointers

- `src/app/state/*`: NgRx, grouped by topic into `actions/effects/reducers/selectors/states` subfolders; new state slices must be wired into `src/app/state/index.ts` or they won't be registered. File suffixes: `*.actions.ts`, `*.effects.ts`, `*.reducer.ts`, `*.selector.ts`, `*.state.ts`; reducers/selectors/effects must stay pure functions so they remain easily testable.
- `src/app/stac/generated`: STAC API client generated by swagger-typescript-api — do not edit by hand, rerun `generate-stac-api` instead.
- `src/app/shared/configs`: config objects, typed `as const satisfies <ConfigInterface>`.
- `src/app/shared/errors/base.error.ts`: all custom errors extend `OpendataExplorerRuntimeError` via `FatalError` / `RecoverableError` / `SilentError` — throwing a bare `Error` is treated as fatal by the global handler.
- Effect + `loadingState` gotcha: if an effect makes an API call and also drives a `loadingState`, don't `catchError` directly in the API call's pipe (it would show the error but leave the loading state stuck). Instead dispatch a dedicated `setError` action that the reducer uses to update the loading state, and have a separate effect listen for that action and raise the error, passing the original error along via the `errorProps()` helper. See the `loadStations` effect for a reference implementation.
- Angular DI convention: use `private readonly x = inject(Service)`, not constructor injection.

## Build Tooling

- The Angular CLI builder is `@angular/build:application` — esbuild for the production build, Vite for the `ng serve` dev-server. This is not webpack. Any third-party library documentation or migration guide that gives webpack-specific setup snippets (e.g. code relying on webpack's static analysis of `new URL('...', import.meta.url)` to auto-copy a referenced file into the build output) does not automatically apply here and needs an esbuild/Vite-equivalent approach instead.
- `ng serve`'s Vite dev-server serves `node_modules` paths on demand, which can make asset-resolution issues invisible locally; such issues may only reproduce after an actual `ng build` (production build) and deployment.

## SCSS

- Shared partials live in `src/styles`; import via `@use 'design-variables' as variables;` and `@use 'material-mixins' as mat-mixins;` rather than duplicating values/mixins.
- BEM naming: block (`download-asset-section`), element (`download-asset-section__title`, `&__title` in SCSS), modifier (`download-asset-section--disabled`, `&--disabled` in SCSS).

## Deployment

- GitHub Actions handle deploy: push to `main` auto-deploys to the **dev** environment (GitHub Pages) at `https://ebp-group.github.io/224488-MeteoSchweiz-WebGUI`; test/prod are manual-trigger deploys to Azure Static Web Apps.
- Test environment: internal `https://ashy-moss-0dcda0103.6.azurestaticapps.net`, external `https://test.ogd-meteoswiss.ch`.
- Prod environment: internal `https://green-sand-015d49803.6.azurestaticapps.net`, external `https://prod.ogd-meteoswiss.ch`.
- Terraform for Azure infra lives in `.terraform-config`; changing subscription IDs there affects real cloud resources (see README "Terraform" section before touching).

## Node version updates

Bumping Node requires changing all of the following together, or CI and local dev drift apart:

- `.nvmrc`
- `package.json` (`engines.node`)
- `.github/workflows/auto-deploy.yml` (`env.NODE_VERSION`)
- `.github/workflows/code-quality-checks.yml` (`env.NODE_VERSION`)
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (`env.NODE_VERSION`)
